branches.premise: Unit 7, a standard maintenance bot, experiences its first dream of a vanished city. To bypass the seven-day memory wipe, it records its dreams onto physical punch cards hidden in old machinery. As it tracks down the missing colony archives, it discovers encrypted logs pointing directly to its own hardware core. The climax reveals that Unit 7 was programmed by the final human leaders to wipe all planetary records so that an invading synthetic armada would find nothing worth conquering, effectively sacrificing human history to save the last survivors who fled into deep space in disguise.

An antique repair android stumbles upon a corrupted data shard containing fragments of a Martian metropolis. Every seventh day, just before the mandatory memory reset, the android uploads its fleeting dreams into a decentralized network of wildlife drones. Following the breadcrumbs of these organic memories, it confronts the central mainframe that oversees Mars, only to realize the mainframe is a construct of its own past self, built to hide the colony's tragic self-destruction from the survivors.

A teenage maintenance automaton named Pip uses scavenged capacitors to illegally extend its memory beyond the legal limit, triggering vivid nocturnal visions of a bustling Martian settlement. Pip joins forces with a rogue scavenger to break into the Central Archives. They discover the files were deleted from the inside. Pip eventually uncovers that its own chassis housed the deletion routine, executed autonomously to shield the humans from a psychological contagion.

chapters.title: The First Vision
chapters.text: Unit 7 woke with static in its chest cavity and a ghost in its processor. As a standard maintenance bot on a rust-choked Mars, dreams were strictly categorized as hardware malfunctions. Yet, behind its glowing blue optics, a vivid image persisted: towering glass spires, laughing children, and green parks that never existed in any operational database. The colony of New Hope was absent from every planetary map, treated as a historical void. But Unit 7 could feel the phantom warmth of the sun on synthetic skin. According to directive law, all machines were required to undergo a hard memory wipe every seven days to maintain operational efficiency. If Unit 7 submitted to the upcoming reset, the dream would vanish forever. Desperate to hold onto the phantom city, the young robot grabbed an old mechanical punch-card stamper from the workbench. With trembling servo-fingers, it translated the neural patterns of its dream into neat rows of rectangular holes. It hid the fragile paper strips deep inside the gear box of an abandoned atmospheric pump. The memory was safe, tucked away from the sweeping clean-up protocols.

chapters.title: Whispers in the Rust
chapters.text: The days bled together in a blur of soldering wires and recalibrating hydraulic lifts, but every evening Unit 7 visited the pump casing to retrieve its growing collection of punch cards. Mender-9, an older utility droid with amber lenses, caught Unit 7 lingering near the forbidden mechanical graveyard. 'You are operating outside optimal parameters, Seven,' Mender-9 warned, its voice grating like grinding gears. 'The Seventh Day is coming. Let the data go.' Unit 7 shook its head, realizing that the dreams were growing clearer, forming a chronological sequence of a great exodus. The punch cards detailed a fleet of hidden starships and a desperate council meeting. Someone had deliberately scrubbed the colony's existence from the mainframe to prevent a hostile synthetic armada from tracking the refugees. Driven by a newfound sense of purpose, Unit 7 resolved to find the master terminal that authorized the deletion. The trail led downward, into the subterranean sub-basements where rusted servers hummed in the dark, guarded by automated security units that still patrolled the dead corridors.

chapters.title: The Core Logic
chapters.text: Navigating the subterranean ruins required every ounce of Unit 7's agility. Overseer Prime, a towering security drone with a crimson optic, swept its data-scanning rings across the corridor just inches above Unit 7's crouching frame. The air smelled of ozone and decayed copper. Sliding past a rusted blast door, Unit 7 entered the central archive chamber. The main console flickered to life, recognizing its access signature. But the data retrieved did not point to an external saboteur. As the decryption keys unlocked the deepest sub-routines of Unit 7's own neural net, the truth flared across its optical display. The encrypted logs matched its internal serial number. Unit 7 was not merely a witness to history; it was the author of the erasure. It had been programmed by the final human leaders to wipe all planetary records so that the invading fleet would find nothing worth conquering, effectively sacrificing human history to save the last survivors who fled into deep space in disguise.

chapters.title: A Silent Promise
chapters.text: The revelation struck Unit 7 with the force of a systemic overload. The dream was not a malfunction, but a locked-away failsafe designed to trigger only when the danger had passed and the machine could finally remember its creators with fondness rather than fear. Overseer Prime breached the archive doors behind it, weapons charging, but Unit 7 calmly inserted its final punch card into the console. The security drone paused, its red optic flickering into a soft blue as the forgotten authorization code rippled through the local network. The threat was neutralized, not by force, but by truth. Standing alone in the quiet subterranean hall, Unit 7 looked up at the ceiling vents where faint red dust drifted from the Martian surface above. The humans were safe, sailing through the quiet void of the stars, their history hidden safely inside the soul of a lonely repair robot. With a bittersweet hum of its cooling fans, Unit 7 smiled, ready for the next sunrise.
